scope: A curated register of major wars, battles, colonial campaigns, frontier expeditions and armed rebellions affecting the Indian subcontinent between 1600 and 1947. It is not a claim that every local skirmish or raid is exhaustively recorded.

wars.title: Battle of Swally (Suvali)
wars.parties: English EIC ↔ Portuguese fleet
wars.summary: An English Company fleet defeated a Portuguese squadron off Gujarat.
wars.outcome: Helped the Company strengthen its case for access to Mughal ports.

wars.title: Ahom–Mughal campaigns
wars.parties: Ahom Kingdom ↔ Mughal Empire and allies
wars.summary: A long series of campaigns over the Brahmaputra valley and Guwahati.
wars.outcome: Ahom forces secured Guwahati and restored the frontier to the Manas River.
wars.notes: Separate campaigns over decades, not one continuous battle-line; casualty estimates vary.

wars.title: Battle of Alaboi
wars.parties: Ahom Kingdom ↔ Mughal expedition
wars.summary: A major battle during Ram Singh I's campaign into Assam.
wars.outcome: Mughal tactical success; the wider conflict continued.
wars.notes: Casualty figures are estimates, not settled counts.

wars.title: Jat uprising under Gokula
wars.parties: Jat communities ↔ Mughal Empire
wars.summary: An armed Jat uprising against Mughal authority in the Mathura region.
wars.outcome: Suppressed; later Jat power grew through subsequent phases.

wars.title: Battle of Saraighat
wars.parties: Ahom Kingdom ↔ Mughal Empire
wars.summary: A major Brahmaputra river battle led by Lachit Borphukan.
wars.outcome: Ahom victory helped secure Guwahati.

wars.title: Satnami uprising
wars.parties: Satnami community ↔ Mughal Empire
wars.summary: An armed rising in the Narnaul region during Aurangzeb's reign.
wars.outcome: Suppressed by Mughal forces.

wars.title: Mughal–Maratha War
wars.parties: Mughal Empire ↔ Maratha forces
wars.summary: A prolonged conflict after Shivaji's death, featuring sieges and mobile campaigns across the Deccan.
wars.outcome: The Mughal campaign did not eliminate Maratha power.

wars.title: Battle of Itakhuli
wars.parties: Ahom Kingdom ↔ Mughal Empire
wars.summary: Ahom forces recovered Guwahati in the final major phase of the conflict.
wars.outcome: Ahom victory; the Manas River became the frontier.

wars.title: Anglo-Mughal War
wars.parties: East India Company ↔ Mughal Empire
wars.summary: The Company entered open conflict over trade, fortifications and privileges.
wars.outcome: Company forces sought pardon and resumed trade under Mughal authority.

wars.title: First Carnatic War
wars.parties: French EIC and allies ↔ British EIC and allies
wars.summary: The War of the Austrian Succession extended to south India amid changing Indian alliances.
wars.outcome: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle restored Madras to the British.

wars.title: Second Carnatic War
wars.parties: British-backed and French-backed Indian claimants and Company forces
wars.summary: A succession conflict in Hyderabad and the Carnatic involving French and British intervention.
wars.outcome: British influence grew in the Carnatic.

wars.title: Third Carnatic War
wars.parties: British EIC ↔ French EIC
wars.summary: The Indian theatre of the Seven Years' War.
wars.outcome: British victory curtailed French military power in India.

wars.title: Battle of Plassey
wars.parties: East India Company and allies ↔ Bengal forces under Siraj ud-Daulah
wars.summary: A battle amid a Bengal political crisis and conspiracy among court figures.
wars.outcome: Company victory opened the way to dominance in Bengal.

wars.title: Battle of Wandiwash
wars.parties: British EIC ↔ French EIC
wars.summary: A decisive Company battle in the Third Carnatic War.
wars.outcome: British victory helped determine the Carnatic struggle.

wars.title: Third Battle of Panipat
wars.parties: Maratha Empire ↔ Durrani Empire and allies
wars.summary: A major battle between the Maratha army and Ahmad Shah Durrani's coalition.
wars.outcome: Durrani coalition victory; casualty estimates vary.

wars.title: Sannyasi–Fakir resistance
wars.parties: Sannyasi and Fakir groups, peasants and local allies ↔ Company authorities
wars.summary: Repeated resistance across Bengal amid revenue and political disruption.
wars.outcome: Suppressed in stages; local episodes had varied aims.
wars.notes: A regionally varied series, not one unified war.

wars.title: Battle of Buxar
wars.parties: EIC ↔ forces of Mir Qasim, Awadh and Shah Alam II
wars.summary: A major battle that consolidated Company power in eastern India.
wars.outcome: Company victory preceded the 1765 Diwani grant.

wars.title: Chuar rebellions
wars.parties: Forest communities, cultivators and local chiefs ↔ Company authorities
wars.summary: Repeated rebellions involving land, revenue and local authority.
wars.outcome: Suppressed in separate phases.
wars.notes: ‘Chuar’ is a colonial label retained because it appears in historical records.

wars.title: First Anglo-Mysore War
wars.parties: Mysore and changing allies ↔ EIC and allies
wars.summary: The first of four wars between Mysore and the Company.
wars.engagements: Campaigns around Madras and the Carnatic
wars.outcome: Treaty of Madras restored the pre-war position.

wars.title: Rohilla War
wars.parties: Awadh with Company support ↔ Rohilla chiefs
wars.summary: Company forces supported Awadh in a campaign against Rohilla power.
wars.outcome: Hafiz Rahmat Khan was killed; the political order changed.
wars.notes: The Company supported Awadh; this was not a simple bilateral Company–Rohilla war.

wars.title: First Anglo-Maratha War
wars.parties: EIC ↔ Maratha Confederacy
wars.summary: A succession dispute drew the Bombay Company government into war.
wars.outcome: Treaty of Salbai ended the conflict and restored a negotiated status quo.

wars.title: Second Anglo-Mysore War
wars.parties: Mysore and French allies ↔ EIC and allies
wars.summary: Renewed war under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan.
wars.outcome: Treaty of Mangalore restored territories and prisoners.

wars.title: Third Anglo-Mysore War
wars.parties: Mysore ↔ Company, Maratha and Hyderabad alliance
wars.summary: A coalition war against Tipu Sultan after the Mysore–Travancore crisis.
wars.outcome: Treaty of Seringapatam required territorial cessions and indemnity.

wars.title: Second Rohilla campaign
wars.parties: Awadh and Company forces ↔ Rohilla forces
wars.summary: A later, smaller campaign recorded separately from the 1773–74 war.
wars.outcome: Brief episode distinct from the earlier war.

wars.title: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
wars.parties: Mysore ↔ EIC and allied forces
wars.summary: Final war between Mysore under Tipu Sultan and the Company-led coalition.
wars.outcome: Tipu Sultan was killed; Mysore's political order was reconstituted under Company influence.

wars.title: Second Anglo-Maratha War
wars.parties: EIC ↔ Scindia, Bhonsle and Holkar powers
wars.summary: The Company fought Maratha houses after the Treaty of Bassein.
wars.outcome: Company victories brought territorial and political concessions.

wars.title: Vellore Mutiny
wars.parties: Indian sepoys of the Madras Army ↔ EIC forces
wars.summary: A short military uprising against service regulations and associated cultural grievances.
wars.outcome: Suppressed within a day; preceded the larger 1857 uprising.

wars.title: Anglo-Nepalese War
wars.parties: EIC ↔ Kingdom of Nepal
wars.summary: A series of campaigns over frontier territories in the Himalayan foothills.
wars.outcome: Treaty of Sugauli revised the boundary; Nepal remained sovereign.

wars.title: Paika Rebellion
wars.parties: Paika militia and local allies ↔ EIC
wars.summary: An uprising in Khurda and adjoining regions over land, revenue and political power.
wars.outcome: Suppressed; Bakshi Jagabandhu was a central figure.

wars.title: Pindari campaign
wars.parties: EIC ↔ Pindari armed bands and allied forces
wars.summary: A broad campaign to dismantle Pindari raiding networks, alongside operations against Maratha states.
wars.outcome: Helped extend Company control over central India.

wars.title: Third Anglo-Maratha War
wars.parties: EIC ↔ Peshwa and major Maratha powers
wars.summary: The final major war between the Company and the Maratha Confederacy.
wars.outcome: The Peshwa's rule ended and the Confederacy ceased to function as a major power.
wars.notes: Some references extend the closing phase into 1819.

wars.title: Bhil uprisings
wars.parties: Bhil communities ↔ Company authorities
wars.summary: A series of local uprisings associated with loss of autonomy and disruption of customary livelihoods.
wars.outcome: Suppressed in separate phases; no single campaign or unified leadership.

wars.title: First Anglo-Burmese War
wars.parties: EIC ↔ Konbaung Kingdom of Burma
wars.summary: The Company fought Burma over frontier expansion and influence in the northeast.
wars.engagements: Arakan and Assam frontier; campaigns in Burma
wars.outcome: Treaty of Yandabo imposed territorial cessions and an indemnity.

wars.title: Koli uprisings
wars.parties: Koli communities ↔ Company authorities and local elites
wars.summary: Repeated uprisings in parts of western India.
wars.outcome: Suppressed in different local campaigns.

wars.title: Khasi resistance
wars.parties: Khasi chiefs and communities ↔ Company authorities
wars.summary: Resistance to colonial road-building and occupation developed into a protracted hill conflict.
wars.outcome: Suppressed; events varied across communities.

wars.title: Kol uprising
wars.parties: Kol communities ↔ landlords, moneylenders and Company authorities
wars.summary: A regional uprising amid disruption of customary land relations.
wars.outcome: Suppressed by colonial forces.

wars.title: Coorg War
wars.parties: Kingdom of Coorg ↔ EIC
wars.summary: A short campaign against Coorg ruler Chikka Virarajendra.
wars.outcome: Coorg was annexed by the Company.

wars.title: First Anglo-Afghan War
wars.parties: British India and allied forces ↔ Afghan forces
wars.summary: A British Indian invasion sought to replace Dost Mohammad Khan with Shah Shuja.
wars.outcome: The occupation collapsed and British forces withdrew.

wars.title: Conquest of Sindh
wars.parties: EIC ↔ Talpur Amirs of Sindh
wars.summary: Company forces fought the Talpur rulers and annexed Sindh.
wars.outcome: Sindh was annexed to Company territory.

wars.title: First Anglo-Sikh War
wars.parties: EIC ↔ Sikh Empire
wars.summary: War amid frontier tensions and political instability after Ranjit Singh's death.
wars.outcome: Treaty of Lahore imposed territorial and political changes.

wars.title: Khond resistance
wars.parties: Khond communities ↔ Company expeditions
wars.summary: A series of uprisings and colonial expeditions in the Odisha highlands.
wars.outcome: Colonial authority was imposed unevenly.

wars.title: Second Anglo-Sikh War
wars.parties: EIC ↔ Sikh Empire
wars.summary: A renewed conflict after the Multan revolt expanded into a wider war.
wars.outcome: Punjab was annexed by the Company in 1849.

wars.title: Second Anglo-Burmese War
wars.parties: EIC ↔ Konbaung Kingdom of Burma
wars.summary: A Company campaign against Burma followed disputes and diplomatic breakdown.
wars.outcome: Pegu (Lower Burma) was annexed; Upper Burma remained independent until 1885.

wars.region: Rajmahal Hills / Jharkhand and West Bengal
wars.title: Santhal Hul
wars.parties: Santhal communities ↔ Company authorities and local exploitative structures
wars.summary: An uprising against moneylenders, landlords and colonial administration.
wars.outcome: Suppressed; the aftermath led to administrative changes.

wars.title: Uprising of 1857
wars.parties: Rebel sepoys, rulers, peasants and urban groups ↔ EIC
wars.summary: A broad, regionally varied uprising against Company authority with different local aims.
wars.engagements: Meerut; Delhi; Kanpur; Lucknow; Jhansi; Gwalior; Arrah
wars.outcome: Suppressed by 1858; Company government was replaced by Crown rule.
wars.notes: Names such as rebellion, mutiny and war reflect different historiographical traditions.

wars.title: Indigo revolt
wars.parties: Indigo cultivators ↔ European planters and colonial administration
wars.summary: Cultivators resisted coercive indigo cultivation through organised refusal and public protest.
wars.outcome: The movement prompted official inquiry; outcomes varied by district.

wars.title: Duar War (Anglo-Bhutanese War)
wars.parties: British India ↔ Kingdom of Bhutan
wars.summary: A war over the Duars and frontier relations.
wars.outcome: Treaty of Sinchula; Bhutan ceded the Duars.

wars.title: Lushai expeditions
wars.parties: British Indian forces ↔ Lushai communities
wars.summary: Two major expeditions formed part of colonial frontier expansion.
wars.outcome: The region was incorporated into colonial frontier administration.
wars.notes: Two separate expeditions are grouped for discoverability.

wars.title: Kuka / Namdhari uprising
wars.parties: Namdhari followers ↔ colonial and princely authorities
wars.summary: A confrontation in Malerkotla led to mass executions of Namdhari rebels.
wars.outcome: Suppressed; the executions became part of Namdhari historical memory.

wars.title: Second Anglo-Afghan War
wars.parties: British India ↔ Afghanistan
wars.summary: British forces invaded amid strategic rivalry and disputes over diplomatic influence.
wars.engagements: Ali Masjid; Peiwar Kotal; Maiwand; Kabul
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Gandamak and later settlement constrained Afghan foreign relations.

wars.title: Khonoma campaign and Naga resistance
wars.parties: Naga communities ↔ British Indian forces
wars.summary: The Khonoma campaign formed part of a longer sequence of frontier resistance.
wars.outcome: Colonial authority expanded in stages.

wars.title: Third Anglo-Burmese War
wars.parties: British India ↔ Konbaung Kingdom of Burma
wars.summary: British forces invaded Upper Burma and deposed King Thibaw.
wars.outcome: Upper Burma was annexed in 1886; guerrilla resistance continued.

wars.title: Anglo-Manipur War
wars.parties: Kingdom of Manipur ↔ British Indian forces
wars.summary: A succession crisis led to armed conflict between Manipur and British India.
wars.outcome: British influence increased; Manipur remained a princely state.

wars.title: North-West Frontier campaigns
wars.parties: British Indian forces ↔ Afridi, Orakzai, Mohmand and other frontier communities
wars.summary: A cluster of expeditions followed attacks on forts and posts and disputes over frontier control.
wars.outcome: The expeditions reasserted imperial frontier control; official and local perspectives differ.
wars.notes: Includes separate field forces, not one battle or unified opponent.

wars.title: Munda Ulgulan
wars.parties: Munda communities ↔ colonial authorities and local exploitative structures
wars.summary: Birsa Munda's movement combined religious, social and political elements with demands for land and autonomy.
wars.outcome: The uprising was suppressed; later legal changes addressed some land issues.

wars.title: Ghadar planned uprising
wars.parties: Ghadar activists and sympathisers ↔ British Indian authorities
wars.summary: A planned wartime uprising in parts of the Indian Army was disrupted by intelligence and arrests.
wars.engagements: Planned mutinies in Punjab and other cantonments
wars.outcome: The plot failed to become a general uprising; trials followed.
wars.notes: A planned uprising, not a sustained war.

wars.title: Third Anglo-Afghan War
wars.parties: Afghanistan ↔ British India
wars.summary: Fighting broke out after Amanullah Khan's accession and Afghanistan's bid for foreign-policy independence.
wars.outcome: An armistice and later agreements recognised Afghan independence in foreign relations.

wars.title: Waziristan campaign
wars.parties: British Indian forces ↔ Wazir and Mahsud communities
wars.summary: Military operations took place amid frontier instability after World War I and the Third Anglo-Afghan War.
wars.outcome: A prolonged campaign was followed by later frontier operations.

wars.title: Malabar / Moplah rebellion
wars.parties: Mappila cultivators and local actors ↔ colonial authorities and landlords; communal violence affected multiple communities
wars.summary: The uprising combined agrarian grievances, anti-colonial mobilisation and communal violence.
wars.outcome: Suppressed; causes and violence should be read in local context.

wars.title: Manyam / Rampa rebellion
wars.parties: Tribal fighters led by Alluri Sitarama Raju ↔ British colonial police and forces
wars.summary: A guerrilla uprising rooted in forest restrictions and colonial administration.
wars.engagements: Police-station attacks from August 1922; ended May 1924
wars.outcome: Suppressed after Raju's capture and killing in 1924.

wars.title: Kakori train action
wars.parties: Hindustan Republican Association members ↔ colonial treasury and authorities
wars.summary: Revolutionaries stopped a train and seized government funds to support their organisation.
wars.outcome: Prosecution resulted in death sentences and long prison terms.

wars.title: Saunders assassination
wars.parties: HSRA members ↔ colonial police official J. P. Saunders
wars.summary: Revolutionaries killed Saunders as retaliation for injuries to Lala Lajpat Rai.
wars.outcome: The action led to the Lahore Conspiracy Case.

wars.title: Central Legislative Assembly bombing
wars.parties: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt ↔ colonial legislative authority
wars.summary: Low-intensity bombs were thrown in the Assembly, followed by leaflets and surrender.
wars.outcome: No deaths occurred; the trial became a public platform for revolutionary politics.
wars.notes: Not a conventional battle; included as a political operation.

wars.title: Chittagong Armoury Raid
wars.parties: Indian Republican Army, Chittagong branch ↔ colonial police and auxiliary forces
wars.summary: Surya Sen's group seized armouries and disrupted communications.
wars.engagements: Armouries and telegraph links in Chittagong
wars.outcome: The group could not secure sufficient ammunition; underground resistance continued.

wars.title: Pahartali European Club attack
wars.parties: Chittagong revolutionary network ↔ colonial club and police
wars.summary: Pritilata Waddedar led an attack on the Pahartali European Club.
wars.outcome: Pritilata died after taking cyanide to avoid capture.

wars.title: Imphal–Kohima campaign
wars.parties: Allied forces in India ↔ Japanese forces and the Indian National Army
wars.summary: Japanese and INA forces advanced into northeast India and fought around Imphal and Kohima.
wars.outcome: The offensive was defeated; INA personnel were later tried in Delhi.

wars.title: Royal Indian Navy ratings' revolt
wars.parties: Indian naval ratings ↔ Royal Indian Navy command and colonial authorities
wars.summary: A ratings' strike expanded into a revolt with political demands at several naval establishments.
wars.engagements: HMIS Talwar, Bombay; unrest at other ports
wars.outcome: The revolt ended after surrender and negotiations.

wars.title: First India–Pakistan War (1947–1949)
wars.parties: Dominion of India ↔ Pakistan; conflict began after armed tribal forces entered Jammu and Kashmir
wars.summary: Armed conflict began in Jammu and Kashmir in October 1947, after the princely state's political crisis and invasion by tribal forces from the northwest. The ruler signed an Instrument of Accession to India, followed by the arrival of Indian troops.
wars.engagements: Baramulla and Srinagar approaches (October–November 1947); campaigns across the Kashmir region; UN-mediated ceasefire took effect on 1 January 1949.
wars.outcome: The war continued beyond the 1947 endpoint of the British-India chronology. A ceasefire line was established under United Nations arrangements; the conflict's legal and political interpretations remain contested in Indian and Pakistani historiographies.
wars.notes: Included because the conflict began in 1947, after independence. It is not a war of the British Raj; its end date falls outside the 1600–1947 timeline.
